raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ### What does this PR do? NVFP4 QAT now uses per-token activations, the same scheme as the NVFP4 rollout from #7971. The static per-tensor activation scale is removed. Why per-token: - Each token is quantized with a scale from its own amax, independent of the other tokens in the batch and of earlier training steps. The static scale was a running max of the observed amax, so tokens much smaller than the largest activation seen so far lost block-scale range, and it was 1.0 until the first training step. - Much lower training-inference mismatch in RL training: mean `rollout_corr/k3_kl` over 100 steps 0.060 → 0.0033, the same as native NVFP4 training (see Test). Changes: - `rollout.quantization.moe: NVFP4` always uses per-token activations; `moe_activation` now defaults to `nvfp4_per_token`. - Fake quantization matches FlashInfer's per-token activation quantization and the trainer-side weight export bitwise. - **Breaking:** removes the static NVFP4 refit for SGLang. verl does not support per-token NVFP4 with SGLang yet. - **Breaking:** removes FSDP QAT (`QATLinear`, `QATQuantizer`, `actor.qat` and the FSDP engine's `qat` config). It has been unreachable since #8287: its `w4a16`/`w4a4` modes match no rollout preset, and the FSDP engine has no trainer-side rollout quantizer. QAT requires the Megatron engine. - Merges `nvfp4_qat.md` into `qat.md`. ### Test RL training, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base on DAPO-Math-17k, 8x4 GB200, 100 steps. Routed experts in NVFP4 in training and rollout, layers 0-1 and 44-47 in BF16. Mean over 100 steps: | Training | Rollout activation | `rollout_logprobs_diff_mean` | `k3_kl` | `rollout_is_mean` | |---|---|---|---|---| | NVFP4 QAT, before this PR | static per-tensor | 0.124 | 0.060 | 0.979 | | NVFP4 QAT | per-token | 0.021 | 0.0033 | 0.9996 | | Native NVFP4 training (#7971) | per-token | 0.021 | 0.0033 | 0.9996 | `scripts/rollout_logprob_diff.py` on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Transformer Engine 2.20.2, ModelOpt 0.47. `qat.md` mismatch table setting (EP=8, vLLM TP=2), median of 3 runs: | Rollout | Training | k3_kl | |---|---|---| | NVFP4 MoE | BF16 | 0.00966 | | NVFP4 MoE | NVFP4 QAT | 0.00766 | Unit tests: - new `tests/utils/test_nvfp4_qat_fake_quant_on_gpu.py`: bitwise checks against vLLM / FlashInfer; - updated `tests/utils/test_modelopt_mxfp8_on_gpu.py`: NVFP4 per-token backends; - updated `tests/utils/real_nvfp4/test_nvfp4_per_token_on_cpu.py`. ### API and Usage Example ```yaml actor_rollout_ref: actor: megatron: qat: enable: true mode: nvfp4 rollout: quantization: moe: NVFP4 ``` ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting). - [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). - [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: the GPU tests need Blackwell.

+
+
+def _dequantize(packed: torch.Tensor, block_scale: torch.Tensor, decode: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    packed = packed.view(torch.uint8)
+    codes = torch.stack([packed & 0xF, packed >> 4], dim=-1).flatten(-2).long()
+    values = torch.tensor(_E2M1, device=packed.device)[codes]
+    scale = block_scale.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float().repeat_interleave(16, dim=-1)
+    return values * (scale * decode)

+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)

+    if shape[0] > 1:
+        # Values on the E2M1 rounding ties once scaled by the block maximum.

+    if shape[0] > 2:

+    if shape[0] > 3 and shape[1] >= 32:
